title: Domains: a strongly transcendental generator kills quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $R\subseteq S$ be a subring of a commutative ring with $R$ and $S$ integral domains (nonzero rings without zero divisors). Let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strongly-transcendental] (for the inclusion $R\to S$; for domains this says that $a_0+a_1x+\dots+a_kx^k=0$ with $a_i\in R$ forces all $a_i=0$), and assume that $S$ is a finitely generated module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] over the subring $R[x]\subseteq S$ generated by $R$ and $x$ (so $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]). Then $R\to S$ is not quasi-finite at any prime ideal of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].
